name: MAURITANIA

flag.title: Green & Gold
flag.note: Star & crescent on green, red border bands

lead: Mauritania is a huge Sahara country. Desert covers nine-tenths of it. A train nearly 3 km long hauls iron ore. A giant rock ring seen from space looks like an eye.
geo: Mauritania has endless dunes, flat gravel plains and rocky plateaus. Canyons cut through the Adrar plateau, and date palms shade its oases.
Cool ocean currents meet the desert on the Atlantic coast, filling lagoons with fish and seabirds. The Senegal River in the south is the one green strip.
animals: The fennec fox's ears are bigger than its head. They hear beetles under the sand and shed desert heat.
Flamingos, pelicans and spoonbills pack the mudflats of Banc d'Arguin National Park in winter.
culture: Mauritanian culture mixes Arab, Berber and West African ways. Families share a huge bowl of lamb and rice and eat with their hands.
Mint tea is brewed three times and poured from a height to make froth. Drinking all three glasses shows respect.
history: Mauritania lay on the trans-Saharan trade routes. Chinguetti became one of Islam's seven holy cities. Its private libraries kept thousands of old manuscripts.
France colonised the land in the early 1900s. Mauritania became independent on 28 November 1960. Today it earns money from iron ore, offshore gas and Atlantic fish.
wows: The 40-km-wide Eye of the Sahara helps astronauts find their way.
The iron-ore train can haul 17,000 tonnes.
Chinguetti has 13 private libraries with about 6,000 manuscripts, some from the 8th century.
Over two million migratory birds winter at Banc d'Arguin.
Mauritania's Atlantic waters are great fishing grounds, supplying about 20% of its exports.
Kediet Ijill, the highest peak, is almost solid iron ore.
Nouakchott grew from a village of hundreds in 1957 to 1.6 million people.

myths.myth: The Sahara is the world's biggest desert
myths.fact: Antarctica is bigger. The Sahara is the biggest hot desert.
Winter nights there can fall below freezing. Sand loses its heat fast.
